meta.subtitle: Diagnostics and biopharma lab leader growing mid-single digits with widening margins, weighed against OBBBA and PAMA reimbursement risk

analystCommentary: Labcorp trades at $303.98, against a consensus target of $344.81 (+13.4%) and an 18-analyst split of Buy 13 · Hold 4 · Sell 1. Second-quarter 2026 revenue reached $3.73 billion, up 5.8%, with operating income of $451.6 vs. $394.5 a year earlier and margin of 12.1%, up 90 bps. Adjusted EPS was $4.99 vs. $4.35, up 14.9%. Management lifted full-year guidance, taking enterprise revenue growth to 5.4% to 6.3% and adjusted EPS to $18.10 to $18.55. We rate the shares BUY. The base case lands near the consensus target and the $352.50 median; the bull case carries the target range to the top of the Street range of $293.00–$385.00. The bear case rests on OBBBA-driven utilization loss and further PAMA reimbursement cuts. At 25.1x trailing earnings and 16.6x the next twelve months, the multiple is full, but mid-single-digit organic growth and margin gains in both segments support it.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Labcorp Holdings Inc. provides laboratory services through two operating segments, Diagnostics Laboratories and Biopharma Laboratory Services. The company was founded in 1995 and is headquartered in Burlington, North Carolina. Its diagnostics menu spans blood chemistry, urinalysis, thyroid, PSA, and infectious-disease testing, alongside specialty gene-based and esoteric testing in oncology, cardiovascular disease, and women's health. Biopharma Laboratory Services supports pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device customers through central laboratory and early development work. Labcorp employs nearly 71,000 people, serves clients in approximately 100 countries, and performed more than 750 million tests. It provided support for more than 85% of the new drugs and therapeutic products approved by the FDA in 2025. FY25 revenue was $14B, up 7.2%, with net income of $876.5M and diluted EPS of $10.46. The business splits into a larger Diagnostics Laboratories segment and a smaller Biopharma Laboratory Services segment.

thesis.body: Labcorp is a scale diagnostics and biopharma-services provider growing revenue in the mid-single digits while expanding margin. Second-quarter 2026 revenue rose 5.8% to $3,731.1, with organic revenue of 4.2%, acquisitions net of divestitures of 1.2%, and foreign currency of 0.4%. Operating income margin widened 90 bps to 12.1%, and adjusted EPS grew 14.9% to $4.99. Diagnostics Laboratories revenue rose 5.5% and Biopharma Laboratory Services rose 6.5%. Adjusted-EPS guidance was raised to $18.10 to $18.55, and enterprise revenue-growth guidance to 5.4% to 6.3%. The counter-case is regulatory: OBBBA could reduce insurance coverage and diagnostics utilization, and PAMA reimbursement cuts resume in 2027. At 25.1x trailing earnings, the valuation leaves limited room for a growth or reimbursement disappointment.

catalysts: Management raised both full-year revenue-growth and adjusted-EPS guidance, up 30 basis points and 30 cents at the midpoint.
A $1.0 billion increase in the share repurchase authorization, bringing the remaining total authorization to $1.4 billion.
Biopharma Laboratory Services visibility, with a TTM book-to-bill of 1.03 on a backlog of $8.73 billion and next-twelve-months forecast backlog conversion of $2.75 billion.
Adjusted operating income margin expanded 70 bps to 15.8%, a sign that efficiency programs are landing.
Bolt-on acquisitions added 1.9% to Diagnostics Laboratories revenue growth in the quarter.
risks: OBBBA changes to Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act could reduce insurance coverage and diagnostics utilization; the company continues to evaluate the impact through 2028.
Medicare reimbursement under PAMA is set to fall further once the current-year freeze lifts.
Early Development revenue fell 1.4% and backlog rose only 0.2% year over year, a biopharma soft spot the risk section develops.
Quarterly free cash flow can be lumpy, driven by working-capital timing and capital-spending cycles.
The forward multiple of 16.6x leaves little cushion for a growth or reimbursement miss.

financials.incomeCommentary: Second-quarter 2026 revenue was $3,731.1, up 5.8% from $3,527.3, driven by organic revenue of 4.2%, acquisitions net of divestitures of 1.2%, and foreign currency of 0.4%. Diagnostics Laboratories revenue was $2,900.7, up 5.5%, on requisition volume up 3.0% and price/mix up 2.5%. Biopharma Laboratory Services revenue was $836.2, up 6.5%, with Central Labs up 9.8% and Early Development down 1.4%. Operating income rose to $451.6 from $394.5, and operating income margin widened 90 bps to 12.1%. Adjusted operating income was $588.7 vs. $531.6, a 15.8% margin, up 70 bps. Net earnings attributable to Labcorp were $298.7 vs. $237.9, and diluted EPS was $3.64 vs. $2.84. Adjusted EPS was $4.99 vs. $4.35, up 14.9%. Over five years the pattern is one of recovery: revenue grew from $13.0B in FY24 to $14.0B in FY25, up 7.2%, while operating margin rebuilt from 6.0% in FY23 to 9.9% in FY25 following the Fortrea spin-off.
financials.balanceCommentary: At the end of the second quarter of 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $141.8 million and total debt was $5.86 billion. In June the company retired $500.0 million in senior notes. On a full-year basis, FY25 total debt was $5.6B and net debt was $5.1B against total equity of $8.6B. Net debt to EBITDA on a trailing basis is 2.6x and interest coverage is 6.6x, consistent with an investment-grade profile. The current ratio was 1.80 on a trailing basis and 1.42 at FY25. Leverage is moderate for a cash-generative diagnostics business, and maintenance of the investment-grade rating is called out as a risk factor tied to leverage-ratio covenants under the revolving credit facility.
financials.cashflowCommentary: Second-quarter 2026 operating cash flow was $445.5 vs. $620.6 a year earlier, and free cash flow was $313.9 vs. $542.7; management attributes the decline to working capital timing and planned increases in capital expenditures. Capital expenditures rose to $131.6 from $77.9. For the six months, operating cash flow was $637.0 vs. $639.1 and free cash flow was $384.4 vs. $435.2. Full-year 2026 free cash flow guidance is $1,240 to $1,360. FY25 free cash flow was $1.2B on an 8.6% FCF margin, and the trailing FCF yield is 4.7%.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: Labcorp trades at 25.1x trailing earnings, 1.7x sales, and 13.8x EV/EBITDA, with a forward P/E of 16.6x on the next twelve months and roughly 15.3x on FY27 estimates. The trailing multiple is elevated relative to the company's mid-single-digit revenue growth, but the forward multiple compresses as adjusted earnings step up. Consensus estimates call for FY26E revenue of $14.7B and EPS of $18.35, and FY27E revenue of $15.5B and EPS of $19.84. The Street rates the shares Buy, 13 of 18 analysts, with a consensus target of $344.81, a median of $352.50, and a range of $293.00–$385.00. Against the $303.98 price, the consensus implies +13.4%. The dividend yield is 0.95%.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Enterprise revenue growth reaches the top of raised guidance at 6.3% and adjusted EPS lands near $18.55, with margin expansion continuing across both segments. As OBBBA and PAMA fears fade, the forward multiple re-rates higher, carrying the shares to the top of the Street's target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Revenue grows within the raised guidance range and consensus FY27 earnings are met, with the forward multiple roughly held. The outcome sits near the Street's consensus and median price targets. Mid-single-digit organic growth and steady margin gains, not multiple expansion, drive the return.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Coverage losses from OBBBA and resuming PAMA rate cuts squeeze Diagnostics volume and pricing. Biopharma demand stays soft, with the Early Development contraction and near-flat backlog persisting. The multiple de-rates toward the lower half of the 52-week range of $244.52 – $341.80.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: We weight the base case at 45%, the bull at 30%, and the bear at 25%. The probability-weighted fair value sits above today's price and below the consensus target, consistent with a BUY rating with a moderate margin of safety. The target range of 315 to 385 brackets the base case and holds above the current price, so the upside line reads positive. The bear case is a real scenario, not a formality: it reflects OBBBA utilization loss and PAMA reimbursement pressure compounding into a mid-teens decline. Reward outweighs risk, but not by a wide margin, which is why the call is BUY rather than a stronger rating.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Labcorp reports one consolidated business built from two operating segments. Diagnostics Laboratories, the larger, contributed $2,900.7 of second-quarter 2026 revenue at an 18.0% adjusted operating income margin, while Biopharma Laboratory Services contributed $836.2 at a 17.0% margin. After intercompany eliminations of (5.8), consolidated revenue was $3,731.1. Diagnostics grew 5.5% in the quarter and Biopharma 6.5%; inside Biopharma, Central Labs advanced 9.8% while Early Development slipped 1.4%. The segment offers routine and specialty testing, from blood chemistry to oncology, cardiovascular, and women's health work.

moatFactors.name: Scale and national network
moatFactors.body: Labcorp's advantage starts with scale. A national logistics network and testing volume in the hundreds of millions spread fixed laboratory costs and support a test menu that smaller competitors cannot match. The roughly 71,000-person workforce and dense patient-service footprint are difficult to replicate.

moatFactors.name: Specialty and esoteric testing
moatFactors.body: The specialty menu spans gene-based and esoteric testing in oncology, cardiovascular disease, and women's health, higher-value work than routine testing. Advances in Labcorp Oncology and new test launches keep extending this mix.

moatFactors.name: Biopharma relationships
moatFactors.body: Deep pharmaceutical relationships underpin Biopharma Laboratory Services: the company supported the large majority of FDA drug approvals in 2025, and a positive book-to-bill with a multi-year backlog gives the segment revenue visibility.

moatFactors.name: Reimbursement exposure
moatFactors.body: Moat durability is capped by payer power. The commercial laboratory business competes intensely on price, and Medicare rates set under PAMA continue to ratchet lower.

businessMoat.durability: The moat is real but narrow. Scale, a national network, and entrenched biopharma relationships give Labcorp durable cost and breadth advantages, but the commercial laboratory business is intensely competitive on price and exposed to payer and government reimbursement. Margin is still expanding, which shows pricing and efficiency have room to run, yet PAMA-driven reimbursement cuts and OBBBA coverage changes could erode testing utilization over time. We judge the moat narrow rather than wide.

points: Enterprise revenue guidance for 2026 was raised to $14,710 to $14,827, growth of 5.4% to 6.3%, off 2025 enterprise revenue of $13,952.
Consensus sees FY26E revenue of $14.7B rising to FY27E revenue of $15.5B, with EPS advancing from $18.35 to $19.84.
Diagnostics Laboratories volume grew 3.0% with price/mix of 2.5% in the quarter, and bolt-on acquisitions added 1.9% to segment revenue.
Biopharma Laboratory Services 2026 guidance is $3,269 to $3,300, growth of 5.5% to 6.5%, led by Central Labs even as Early Development lags, the soft spot covered under risks.
New oncology and consumer offerings, including the nationwide launch of ColoSense and the Marker by Labcorp genetic health panel, extend the test menu.

management.leadership: Adam Schechter is Chairman and CEO of Labcorp. On the second-quarter results he described 6% revenue growth, margin expansion, and double-digit adjusted EPS growth, and pointed to expanded leadership in oncology and specialty testing. The Board combines the Chair and CEO roles, with an independent Lead Independent Director in place since 2009 to provide independent oversight. Management raised full-year guidance alongside the quarter, a signal of confidence in the second-half outlook.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation is balanced between reinvestment, M&A, and returns. In the second quarter of 2026 the company invested $225.7 million in acquisitions, repurchased $353.8 million of stock, and paid $58.7 million in dividends, and it retired $500.0 million in senior notes in June. The Board approved a $1.0 billion increase in the share repurchase authorization, bringing the remaining total to $1.4 billion, and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.72 per share. FY25 free cash flow was $1.2B and 2026 guidance is $1,240 to $1,360, which comfortably funds the dividend and buyback. Net debt to EBITDA of 2.6x leaves room for continued bolt-on acquisitions.
management.governance: Governance rests on the DEF 14A proxy statement dated 2026-04-10. Other than Mr. Schechter, all current Board members and all nominees for director qualify as independent under NYSE listing standards. The Chair and CEO roles are combined, offset by a Lead Independent Director maintained since 2009. The Audit Committee reviews related-party transactions, and the company reported no transactions considered related-party transactions since January 1, 2025. Non-employee directors received an annual retainer of $120,000 in 2025. The combined Chair/CEO structure is the main governance watch-item, mitigated by the independent-director majority and Lead Independent Director.

idiosyncratic: Reimbursement is the central idiosyncratic exposure. Medicare rates set under PAMA have already fallen for many tests; reductions are frozen for 2026 but capped at 15% per year for 2027-2029, a multi-year headwind to Diagnostics pricing.
The OBBBA law, enacted July 4, 2025, is the key regulatory unknown; management currently assesses no likely material impact but continues to monitor the effect on coverage and testing volumes.

Biopharma demand is uneven: Central Labs is growing while Early Development contracts, and total backlog is barely higher than a year ago, so a pullback in pharma R&D spending would pressure the segment.
Cash conversion can swing sharply, as the quarter's free cash flow drop to $313.9 from $542.7 alongside capital expenditures of $131.6 shows.
risks.systemic: Systemic risks are macroeconomic and regulatory. Significant changes in global economic conditions, inflation, and credit-market volatility could reduce testing volumes, biopharma demand, and cash collections, and raise the cost of credit. Labcorp depends on government and third-party payer reimbursement, so federal budget pressure and healthcare-policy shifts weigh on a portion of revenue. The company carries FY25 net debt of $5.1B and relies on maintaining its investment-grade rating and leverage covenants under its revolving credit facility. Foreign-currency movements also affect results, given operations in approximately 100 countries.

body: We rate Labcorp BUY with a target range of 315 to 385, bracketing a base case near the consensus target of $344.81 and the $352.50 median. The investment case is a steady compounder: mid-single-digit organic revenue growth, expanding margins, and disciplined capital returns, bought at a full but not extreme multiple. On our probability weighting the expected return is positive and reward exceeds downside, though the margin of safety is moderate.

We take the downside seriously. Coverage erosion under OBBBA and further PAMA rate cuts could compress both volumes and the multiple, driving a mid-teens decline from the current $303.98. That is why we weight the bear at 25% and hold the rating at BUY rather than a stronger call. At 25.1x trailing and 16.6x forward earnings, we would add on weakness rather than chase strength.
